gotchas: Unknown fields are discarded silently, so a misspelled field name in a hand-edited config is ignored rather than reported.
CheckDuplicateAccessKey checks identities only, not service accounts.

weed/filer/abstract_sql/.character: The shared implementation behind the MySQL, Postgres and SQLite filer stores, with optional one-table-per-bucket layout
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.what: AbstractSqlStore implements FilerStore on database/sql through a SqlGenerator each dialect supplies. Rows are keyed by (hash of directory, name, directory) with the encoded entry as the value (gzipped when it has more than 50 chunks on insert). With SupportBucketTable, paths under /buckets/<bucket>/ live in a table named after the bucket, created on first use and dropped when the bucket's children are deleted, so deleting a bucket is one DROP TABLE. Transactions are a *sql.Tx carried in the context under 'tx' (read committed). KV rows live in the default table, keyed by the first 8 bytes of the key and its base64 rest, optionally on a separate small connection pool (a quarter of max connections, at most 8). ScanEntries reads a subtree in one repeatable-read read-only transaction, across bucket tables when scanning / or /buckets, refusing when the store has a single connection. Retryable errors are retried outside transactions.
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.why: Consequence: SQL stores are what multi-filer clusters share, so their key layout decides listing order and bucket-delete cost. Design: per-bucket tables make bucket deletion O(1) and keep one bucket's rows out of another's index; KV gets its own pool so a burst of metadata queries cannot starve lock and offset writes.
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.when: Filers configured with mysql, mysql2, postgres, postgres2 or sqlite.
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.ux: Fast bucket deletes with the per-bucket-table variants.
weed/filer/abstract_sql/.if_broken: Entries vanish into the wrong table, bucket deletes leave rows, or the connection pool deadlocks.
gotchas: The bucket routing hardcodes /buckets/ instead of the filer's DirBucketsPath, and accepts bucket names by the lenient VerifyS3BucketName (non-ASCII names become table names).
Insert falls back to update only when the error text contains 'duplicate entry' (MySQL wording); KvPut falls back to update on any insert error.
UpdateEntry does not gzip large chunk lists the way InsertEntry does, and an UPDATE that matches no row reports success.
A transaction left open (see the StreamRenameEntry issue) keeps its pooled connection until the filer restarts, since the wrapper begins it on a context that is never cancelled.

weed/filer/filechunks.go.character: Chunk-list arithmetic: sizes, ETags, garbage detection, chunk differences and the chunk views a read needs
weed/filer/filechunks.go.what: TotalSize is the furthest chunk end; FileSize takes the larger of that and the stored size (and the remote size when the remote is newer). ETag returns the stored MD5, else ETagChunks: a single chunk's MD5, or the multipart form md5(concat(chunk md5s))-N. CompactFileChunks resolves manifests, computes visible intervals and splits chunks into those still visible and garbage fully overwritten by newer ones; MinusChunks resolves both lists (data and manifest chunks) and returns what the old list has that the new one does not, which is what the filer deletes on an update. ViewFromChunks / ViewFromVisibleIntervals cut the visible intervals into ChunkViews (file id, offset in chunk, view size and offset, cipher key, gzip flag) for a byte range; MergeIntoVisibles and MergeIntoChunkViews add one chunk to existing lists.
weed/filer/filechunks.go.why: Consequence: SeaweedFS files are lists of possibly overlapping chunks where the newest write wins; every read and every chunk deletion depends on computing which bytes of which chunk are visible. Design: the newest ModifiedTsNs wins per byte range, so overwrites need no rewrite of older chunks, and a chunk becomes garbage only when nothing of it is visible.
weed/filer/filechunks.go.when: Every read path (S3 GET through the gateway's own reader uses these too), CreateEntry/UpdateEntry chunk cleanup, rename overwrite cleanup.
weed/filer/filechunks.go.ux: Correct bytes after overwrites and partial writes from mounts.
weed/filer/filechunks.go.if_broken: Reads return old data or wrong offsets, or still-visible chunks are deleted.
gotchas: ETagChunks gives a multi-chunk object a multipart-style ETag ('-N') even when it was written in one PUT; the S3 gateway avoids this by storing its own ETag and MD5.

weed/filer/filechunks_read.go.character: The sweep that turns overlapping chunks into non-overlapping visible intervals
weed/filer/filechunks_read.go.what: readResolvedChunks makes a start and an end point per chunk inside the range, sorts them by offset then timestamp, and sweeps with a queue ordered by timestamp: at each point the newest active chunk owns the bytes since the previous point. The result is an IntervalList of VisibleIntervals, each naming the chunk, its offset in the chunk, size, cipher key and gzip flag.
weed/filer/filechunks_read.go.why: Design: one O(n log n) sweep instead of repeated interval insertion; it is the basis of CompactFileChunks and every read.
weed/filer/filechunks_read.go.if_broken: Overlapping writes read back the wrong version of a byte range.
gotchas: Chunks are told apart by ModifiedTsNs: two overlapping chunks with the same timestamp make the end-point removal ambiguous (it removes the first queued point with that timestamp).
The sort comparator converts int64 differences to int, which truncates on 32-bit builds.
A manifest chunk reaching it only prints a warning to stdout; callers must resolve manifests first.

weed/filer/interval_list.go.character: A doubly linked list of non-overlapping intervals with newest-wins insertion
weed/filer/interval_list.go.what: IntervalList keeps intervals between sentinel head and tail. AppendInterval adds at the end (callers append in order). InsertInterval places an interval and, where it overlaps existing ones, keeps whichever has the newer timestamp, splitting and cloning values (SetStartStop adjusts each value's own offsets). Overlay replaces a range unconditionally. Len counts intervals.
weed/filer/interval_list.go.why: Design: generic over the value (VisibleInterval, ChunkView) so visible intervals and chunk views share the split logic; incremental insertion lets a mount add a freshly written chunk without recomputing the whole file.
weed/filer/interval_list.go.when: Visible-interval and chunk-view lists in reads and in FileChunkSection.addChunk.
weed/filer/interval_list.go.if_broken: Interval lists with gaps or overlaps, hence wrong reads.
gotchas: Overlay shares the split pieces' values with the original instead of cloning and re-offsetting them; nothing outside tests calls it.
Front() and traversal do not take the list's lock; readers such as ChunkReadAt hold Lock.RLock themselves.

weed/filer/filechunk_manifest.go.character: Chunk manifests: folding long chunk lists into manifest chunks, resolving them back, and the retrying whole-chunk fetch
weed/filer/filechunk_manifest.go.what: ResolveChunkManifest expands manifest chunks overlapping a byte range into their data chunks (and returns the manifest chunks themselves), fetching manifests in parallel with 4 workers plus overflow goroutines, cancelling the batch on the first failure and recursing into nested manifests. resolveOneChunkManifest fetches and unmarshals one manifest, optionally through a ChunkManifestCache. fetchWholeChunk and retriedStreamFetchChunkData read a chunk from its locations, reachable ones first, resuming at the byte already written, with backoff (1 s growing by half up to util.RetryWaitTime) and a retry on fresh locations when every URL fails. MaybeManifestize first folds 256 or more chunks under 1 MiB into manifests of 256 (foldSmallChunks), then folds every full batch of ManifestBatch data chunks into one manifest chunk (mergeIntoManifest: saves the serialized list as a chunk spanning min..max offset); on failure it deletes the manifests it saved and returns the input list.
weed/filer/filechunk_manifest.go.why: Consequence: an entry's whole chunk list is one store value, and stores cap value size; a large or long-appended file would stop being writable. Design: one level of folding, small chunks first because many tiny chunks (appends) bloat the list fastest; the input list is still a correct entry if folding fails.
weed/filer/filechunk_manifest.go.when: CreateEntry/UpdateEntry chunk cleanup, AppendToEntry, the filer's autochunk and zip-extract writes, WebDAV, the gateway's chunk manifest path, shell fs.distribute.chunks; resolution on every read.
weed/filer/filechunk_manifest.go.ux: Very large files and append-heavy logs remain writable.
weed/filer/filechunk_manifest.go.if_broken: Large files fail to save, or manifests resolve to the wrong chunk set (data loss on the next cleanup).
gotchas: Every chunk read appends readDeleted=true, so a needle already deleted on the volume server is still served while its space is not reclaimed.
On a failed resolution ResolveChunkManifest returns the data chunks resolved before the failing slot together with the error; callers must not use them as the full list.
mergeIntoManifest moves the data chunks' FileId strings into Fid (BeforeEntrySerialization) in place.

weed/filer/filechunk_manifest_cache.go.character: A small LRU of fetched manifest bytes with request coalescing
weed/filer/filechunk_manifest_cache.go.what: ChunkManifestCache keeps manifest blobs keyed by file id, cipher key and compression flag, bounded by entry count and bytes (mounts use 256 entries / 64 MiB), returns copies, and coalesces concurrent fetches of one manifest through singleflight while letting each caller give up on its own context.
weed/filer/filechunk_manifest_cache.go.why: Consequence: a mount reopening the same large file re-fetched every manifest each time. Design: manifests are immutable needles, so caching by file id is safe.
weed/filer/filechunk_manifest_cache.go.ux: Faster opens of large files in mounts.
weed/filer/filechunk_manifest_cache.go.if_broken: Repeated manifest fetches, or stale manifests if a file id were ever reused.

weed/filer/filechunk_section.go.character: A 64 MiB slice of a file's chunks with its own visible intervals, chunk views and reader
weed/filer/filechunk_section.go.what: FileChunkSection holds the chunks overlapping one 64 MiB section. addChunk merges a newly written chunk into the section's visible intervals and chunk views incrementally and drops chunks it fully hides. setupForRead builds visible intervals and chunk views lazily on first read and a ChunkReadAt over them; readDataAt reads through it. DataStartOffset and NextStopOffset answer SEEK_DATA / SEEK_HOLE within the section.
weed/filer/filechunk_section.go.why: Consequence: recomputing visibility over a whole large file on every write or read was too slow for mounts. Design: sections bound the work to the region touched.
weed/filer/filechunk_section.go.when: weed mount's file handles through ChunkGroup.
weed/filer/filechunk_section.go.ux: Mount reads and writes on large files stay fast; lseek SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE work.
weed/filer/filechunk_section.go.if_broken: Mount reads return stale bytes after writes, or seek reports wrong holes.
gotchas: removeGarbageChunks matches chunks by their FileId string, which is only populated after GetFileIdString ran on them.

weed/filer/filechunk_group.go.character: A file's chunks organized as sections, with parallel reads and hole search, for weed mount
weed/filer/filechunk_group.go.what: NewChunkGroup builds a reader cache (2 x concurrent readers, at least 32 downloaders) and sets the chunks: SetChunks resolves top-level manifest chunks (through the manifest cache) and distributes data chunks to 64 MiB sections. AddChunk adds a written chunk to every section it touches. ReadDataAt reads a range sequentially or, across several sections, in parallel (up to the concurrent-reader limit, 16 by default, capped at 128), zero-filling sections with no chunks; a manifest resolution failure is returned on every read. SearchChunks implements SEEK_DATA and SEEK_HOLE.
weed/filer/filechunk_group.go.why: Design: per-section state lets concurrent reads of different regions proceed without one lock over the whole file, and lets writes update only the sections they touch.
weed/filer/filechunk_group.go.when: Every open file in weed mount.
weed/filer/filechunk_group.go.ux: Throughput of large sequential and parallel reads in mounts.
weed/filer/filechunk_group.go.if_broken: Mount reads stall, return zeros for data, or fail after one transient manifest error.
gotchas: SetChunks resolves one level of manifests with context.Background(); a manifest found inside a manifest would be treated as a data chunk.
A failed manifest resolution is remembered (resolveErr) until the next successful SetChunks, so every read fails meanwhile.

weed/filer/reader_at.go.character: ChunkReadAt: io.ReaderAt over chunk views, with parallel chunk reads, zero-filled holes and prefetch; and LookupFn, a cached volume lookup over a filer client
weed/filer/reader_at.go.what: doReadAt maps a read to tasks per chunk view and gaps to zero-fill, reads the tasks sequentially (one task, or a random access pattern) or in parallel (at least 4), and on a sequential pattern asks the reader cache to prefetch the next chunk views. Small reads of range-fetchable chunks (unencrypted, uncompressed) go straight to the chunk cache or a ranged fetch; others read the whole chunk through the shared ReaderCache, caching it when it fits the chunk cache's part limit. EOF is returned when the read reaches the file size. LookupFn resolves a file id's volume through the filer's LookupVolume, caches up to 10,000 volumes, orders same-data-center and locally stored (not remote-tiered) replicas first and shuffles within each group.
weed/filer/reader_at.go.why: Design: whole-chunk reads with caching suit sequential workloads, ranged reads suit random ones; ReaderPattern decides. Holes read as zeros, matching POSIX sparse files.
weed/filer/reader_at.go.when: Mount reads (via FileChunkSection), filer HTTP and other readers built with NewChunkReaderAtFromClient; LookupFn in clients that only have a filer connection (sftp, replication sources, ChunkStreamReader).
weed/filer/reader_at.go.ux: Read latency and throughput in mounts and gateways.
weed/filer/reader_at.go.if_broken: Short or corrupted reads, or reads that keep hitting a volume server that moved.
gotchas: LookupFn's volume cache is never invalidated: a volume that moves keeps resolving to its old locations for the life of the closure (fetches still retry other replicas).

weed/filer/reader_cache.go.character: Shared per-file downloader cache: one in-flight whole-chunk download per file id, with pinning, eviction and prefetch
weed/filer/reader_cache.go.what: ReaderCache maps file ids to SingleChunkCachers. readChunkAt joins an existing download, else reads the persistent chunk cache, else starts a download (evicting the oldest finished downloader, preferring unpinned ones, when at the limit) and waits for it. A stream (one reader positioned in a chunk) pins the chunk it is in; a downloader is dropped once fully consumed or left by its last stream, or on error so the next read retries. MaybeCache starts prefetch downloads for the next chunk views. SingleChunkCacher runs on its own context, cancelled once no reader or stream can use it any more (consumed, left by its last stream, or dropped by destroy, which cancels unheld downloads instead of waiting for them, #12616); it reserves memory from the optional ReaderCacheBudget, looks up and fetches the whole chunk (retrying on fresh locations), stores it in the chunk cache when asked, and serves slices to readers.
weed/filer/reader_cache.go.why: Consequence: sequential readers would download each chunk once per read call, and concurrent readers of one file would download it many times. Design: share the download, keep a chunk only while a stream is in it, and bound memory.
weed/filer/reader_cache.go.when: ChunkReadAt reads and prefetch in mounts and other chunk readers.
weed/filer/reader_cache.go.if_broken: Memory blowups from undropped chunk buffers, repeated downloads, or reads blocked behind a dead download.
gotchas: A download is shared, so it runs on its own context rather than a reader's: a reader that gives up only stops waiting, and the download is cancelled only when no reader or stream holds it. Its volume re-lookups ignore even that context, because concurrent lookups of one volume are coalesced and a cancelled download must not fail the others (#12616).
A failed download is removed only when the next reader notices the completed error, so the first reader after a failure pays a retry.

weed/filer/reader_cache_budget.go.character: Memory budget shared by reader caches: reservations, idle eviction and waiting
weed/filer/reader_cache_budget.go.what: ReaderCacheBudget (default 256 MiB) reserves a downloader's allocation before it fetches; when full it evicts idle (completed) downloaders, unpinned first, and otherwise waits for a release or completion, or until the download is cancelled; a cancelled download never evicts a chunk for itself (#12616). canFit tells callers when a chunk cannot fit at all, so they range-fetch instead. A chunk larger than the whole budget is an error.
weed/filer/reader_cache_budget.go.why: Consequence: many open files each prefetching whole chunks could exhaust a mount's memory. Design: one budget across files, evicting finished buffers before waiting.
weed/filer/reader_cache_budget.go.when: Reader caches created with a budget (weed mount's -readerCacheSizeMB).
weed/filer/reader_cache_budget.go.ux: Bounded mount memory under many concurrent readers.
weed/filer/reader_cache_budget.go.if_broken: OOM in mounts, or reads that wait forever for budget.
gotchas: The wait has no timeout of its own: a reservation waits as long as every reserved chunk is an in-flight download that some reader still holds.

weed/filer/reader_pattern.go.character: Sequential-versus-random access detection for a reader
weed/filer/reader_pattern.go.what: MonitorReadAt tracks the furthest byte read; a read starting within 8 MiB of it counts toward sequential (up to +3), a read further away pushes the counter down, straight to -3 once it is at or below zero. IsRandomMode is a negative counter.
weed/filer/reader_pattern.go.why: Design: hysteresis so one seek does not flip a sequential reader into random mode, and a tolerance wide enough for parallel readahead that arrives slightly out of order.
weed/filer/reader_pattern.go.ux: Prefetch for streaming reads, no wasted downloads for random reads.
weed/filer/reader_pattern.go.if_broken: Random readers download whole chunks they do not need, or sequential readers lose prefetch.

weed/filer/stream.go.character: Streaming file content to a writer, and ChunkStreamReader, an io.ReadSeeker / ReaderAt over a chunk list
weed/filer/stream.go.what: PrepareStreamContentWithThrottler resolves visible chunk views for a range, looks every chunk's locations up first (with a short backoff), then returns a function that writes the range: zeros for gaps, each chunk via retriedStreamFetchChunkData, a retry on fresh locations when a chunk failed before writing anything, optional bandwidth throttling. PrepareStreamContentWithPrefetch does the same with several chunks fetched ahead through pipes (stream_prefetch.go). StreamContent is the unthrottled form. Read JWTs come from jwt.signing.read.key (or the filer JWT when reading through the filer proxy). ChunkStreamReader reads chunk views one at a time into a buffer, keeping up to 16 chunks / 128 MiB of recent buffers, and remembers the first source error (ReaderSourceError). NewFileReader returns inline content or a ChunkStreamReader. IsSameData compares content, or chunk ETags as a multiset.
weed/filer/stream.go.why: Consequence: the filer HTTP read path, the admin file browser and many tools stream files through here. Design: resolve all locations before writing a byte, so a missing volume becomes an error status rather than a truncated 200.
weed/filer/stream.go.when: Filer HTTP GET (with prefetch), admin file browser and Iceberg data preview, filer.conf and other small-file reads (ReadEntry); ChunkStreamReader in replication sinks, sftp, the metadata-log readers, mount sync, the Iceberg worker and the filer's chunk merge.
weed/filer/stream.go.ux: File downloads from the filer and replicated copies of files.
weed/filer/stream.go.if_broken: Truncated downloads, or replicated files that differ from their source.
gotchas: A chunk that fails after some of its bytes were written is not retried, and the error arrives after part of the response is already out.
ChunkStreamReader sizes the stream as the sum of its chunk views and answers io.EOF when the next offset falls in a hole, so a sparse file reads only up to its first hole, without an error.
weed/filer/stream.go.issue_note: ChunkStreamReader silently truncates sparse files. doNewChunkStreamReader sets totalSize to the sum of the chunk views' sizes, ignoring gaps between them and any trailing hole, and prepareBufferFor returns io.EOF when the read offset is not inside a chunk view, so reading stops at the first hole and io.ReadAll reports success. NewFileReader hands this reader to the replication sinks (replication/sink/s3sink/s3_sink.go CreateEntry, and repl_util copyWithDecryption for SSE files), so filer.backup or filer.sync to an S3 sink uploads a file with a hole (created through weed mount by seeking past the end, or extended with truncate -s) cut short at the hole, and the backup reports nothing. Sftp downloads and the Iceberg worker's file reads use the same reader. Reproduced at 917cf534 with a temporary unit test: two chunks [0,10) and [20,30) of a 30-byte file read back 10 bytes, err=nil, SourceError=nil, while FileSize reports 30. The fix is to zero-fill gaps between views and to the entry's file size, as ChunkReadAt.doReadAt and PrepareStreamContentWithThrottler already do.

weed/filer/stream_prefetch.go.character: Prefetched streaming: several chunks fetched ahead through pipes while one is written out
weed/filer/stream_prefetch.go.what: streamChunksPrefetched starts a producer that, for each chunk view, waits for one of prefetchAhead slots, opens a pipe and starts a fetch goroutine writing the chunk into it; the consumer writes zeros for gaps and copies each pipe to the writer in order, retrying a chunk on fresh locations when its fetch failed before writing anything, and throttling if asked. On any failure it cancels the producer and drains every pending pipe before returning.
weed/filer/stream_prefetch.go.why: Consequence: one chunk at a time leaves the link idle during each chunk's first-byte latency. Design: pipes bound prefetch memory to what the writer has not consumed, instead of buffering whole chunks.
weed/filer/stream_prefetch.go.when: Filer HTTP GET when prefetch is configured (PrepareStreamContentWithPrefetch).
weed/filer/stream_prefetch.go.ux: Higher download throughput from the filer.
weed/filer/stream_prefetch.go.if_broken: Out-of-order or truncated downloads, or goroutines left behind after a client disconnects.
gotchas: As in the unprefetched path, a chunk that fails after writing some bytes is not retried.

weed/filer/gateway_upload.go.character: One-chunk upload helper for gateways that write data through a filer connection
weed/filer/gateway_upload.go.what: SaveGatewayDataAsChunk assigns a volume through the filer (collection, replication, TTL, disk type, data center and path from the request), uploads the reader with retries (optionally through the filer's HTTP proxy when volume servers are not directly reachable), and returns the FileChunk at the given offset and timestamp. The filename defaults to the path's last component.
weed/filer/gateway_upload.go.why: Design: one shared implementation of 'assign, upload, build the chunk' for gateways that save data as chunks themselves, with an injectable uploader for tests.
weed/filer/gateway_upload.go.when: The S3 gateway's chunk-manifest saving (s3api_chunk_manifest.go) and WebDAV writes.
weed/filer/gateway_upload.go.if_broken: Manifest chunks or WebDAV writes fail, or land in the wrong collection.

weed/filer/manifest_batch.go.what: ManifestBatch = 10000 data chunks per manifest chunk, for every build without the foundationdb tag.
weed/filer/manifest_batch.go.why: Design: stores reached by this build hold values far larger than a 10,000-chunk list encodes to.
weed/filer/manifest_batch.go.when: MaybeManifestize in every component that folds chunk lists (filer, S3 gateway, mount, WebDAV, shell, filer.copy).
weed/filer/manifest_batch.go.if_broken: Entries too large for the store, or needless manifest reads.
gotchas: The value is a property of the build, not of the configured store; every component folding for one filer must be built the same way.

weed/filer/manifest_batch_foundationdb.g.character: The manifest fold size for FoundationDB builds
weed/filer/manifest_batch_foundationdb.g.what: ManifestBatch = 500 under the foundationdb build tag, because a FoundationDB value stops at 100,000 bytes and a chunk record is about 100 bytes; 500 maximizes how many chunks one fold level can hold (about 250,000, roughly 1 TB at the default chunk size).
weed/filer/manifest_batch_foundationdb.g.why: Consequence: with the default 10,000 the entry was already too large to store before folding ever ran. Design: chosen so the unfolded remainder and the manifest pointers balance.
weed/filer/manifest_batch_foundationdb.g.ux: Files up to about 1 TB on a FoundationDB-backed filer.
weed/filer/manifest_batch_foundationdb.g.if_broken: Large files cannot be saved on FoundationDB.
gotchas: Files beyond about 250,000 chunks would need nested manifests, which MaybeManifestize does not build (author comment).

weed/filer/filer_notify.go.character: Emitting metadata events: commit stamps, the local metadata log buffer and its flush to log files
weed/filer/filer_notify.go.what: NotifyUpdateEvent builds a SubscribeMetadataResponse for an old/new entry pair (skipping the system log directory and contexts marked WithSuppressedMetadataEvents), appends this filer's signature, stamps it with the commit timestamp the mutation reserved (or a fresh one), sends it to the external notification queue if one is configured, appends it to LocalMetaLogBuffer, records it in the request's event sink and runs onMetadataChangeEvent. metaLogInflight hands out strictly increasing stamps and tracks which are still in flight, so LocalDeliveredThroughTsNs / LocalFlushedThroughTsNs can claim a watermark no unannounced mutation lies below. logFlushFunc writes each minute's buffer to /topics/.system/log/<date>/<hh-mm>.<filerId>, in pieces of at most one log-buffer size (lowered when a volume reports a smaller file limit), retrying every 737 ms until it succeeds or shutdown cancels the flush context (then the rest is dropped and counted). ReadPersistedLogBuffer replays those files from a position through an ordered visitor with an 8192-entry readahead, at most 64 replays at once.
weed/filer/filer_notify.go.why: Consequence: every subscriber (S3 gateways, mounts, filer.sync, peer filers) learns changes only through this log; an event stamped below a watermark already claimed would be skipped by readers that trust the watermark. Design: mutations reserve their stamp before the store write and release it if they abort, so the claimed watermark never passes a mutation that may still be announced.
weed/filer/filer_notify.go.when: Every filer mutation; the log buffer flushes every minute.
weed/filer/filer_notify.go.ux: Change propagation latency across gateways and mounts.
weed/filer/filer_notify.go.if_broken: Subscribers miss or reorder events, caches go stale, peers diverge.
gotchas: The external notification queue is called synchronously inside every mutation and its errors are only logged, so a slow queue slows writes and a failing one loses its events.
A metadata-log flush that keeps failing (for example no writable volume) retries forever until shutdown, while the buffer keeps holding the window.

weed/filer/filer_notify_append.go.character: Appending a metadata-log piece to its log file as a new chunk
weed/filer/filer_notify_append.go.what: appendToFile gzips the piece when that saves more than 10%, assigns a volume in the metadata-log collection and replication (filer.options.metaLog.* overrides, then the filer default, then the path rule), uploads it, and commitAppendedChunk appends the chunk at the file's current end with CreateEntry, creating the file if needed. If CreateEntry reports failure but the chunk is in the stored entry, the append is counted as landed; otherwise the uploaded chunk is deleted.
weed/filer/filer_notify_append.go.why: Design: log files are append-only lists of chunks, one per flush piece, so a reader can fetch just the new chunks (the client direct-read path ships chunk refs).
weed/filer/filer_notify_append.go.when: logFlushFunc, once a minute per filer.
weed/filer/filer_notify_append.go.if_broken: Metadata history is lost (subscribers that fall behind cannot catch up) or orphaned log chunks accumulate.
gotchas: The append is a find-then-create without a path lock; it relies on each filer writing its own file name (the filer id suffix).

weed/filer/filer_notify_read.go.character: Reading persisted metadata-log files: ordered replay across filers and chunk refs for client-side reading
weed/filer/filer_notify_read.go.what: collectPersistedLogBuffer lists the day directories from one flush interval before the start, and OrderedLogVisitor merges every filer's minute files in timestamp order with a heap of per-filer iterators (LogFileQueueIterator over LogFileIterator, which reads [4-byte size | LogEntry] records, through the persisted-log cache when possible). CollectLogFileRefs lists the same files as LogFileChunkRefs (chunks, minute, filer id) for clients that read volume servers directly; LastShippedLogEntryTsNsForFiler finds the last timestamp a set of shipped refs covers and whether the last file was complete. HasPersistedLogFiles checks for any day directory at or after a position.
weed/filer/filer_notify_read.go.why: Consequence: a subscriber resuming from a timestamp must see events from every filer that wrote to this store, in order. Design: one file per filer per minute, merged on read; shipping refs lets a client fetch log chunks itself instead of the filer streaming every event.
weed/filer/filer_notify_read.go.if_broken: Resumed subscribers miss or duplicate events.
gotchas: A log chunk that cannot be found (volume deleted or lost) makes the iterator skip the rest of that file with a warning, so its events are never replayed.
Day and minute directories are compared as strings; the layout must stay zero-padded.

weed/filer/filer_on_meta_event.go.character: The filer's own reactions to metadata events: config reloads, bucket hooks, empty-folder tracking and remote tombstones
weed/filer/filer_on_meta_event.go.what: onMetadataChangeEvent runs for every local event and every event applied from a peer: reloads filer.conf when /etc/seaweedfs/filer.conf changes, reloads remote storage configuration and mappings on /etc/remote changes, calls the store's OnBucketCreation / OnBucketDeletion for directories created, deleted or renamed directly under the buckets path, feeds creates, deletes and renames to the empty-folder cleaner (and invalidates its cached bucket policy), and records remote deletions. LoadFilerConf and LoadRemoteStorageConfAndMapping load them at startup.
weed/filer/filer_on_meta_event.go.why: Design: configuration lives in the filer namespace, so watching the event stream makes a change made on any filer take effect on all of them without a restart.
weed/filer/filer_on_meta_event.go.when: Inline in NotifyUpdateEvent and in the meta aggregator's peer event processing.
weed/filer/filer_on_meta_event.go.ux: fs.configure and remote.mount take effect immediately cluster-wide.
weed/filer/filer_on_meta_event.go.if_broken: Storage rules or remote mounts go stale on some filers; per-bucket SQL tables are not created or dropped.
gotchas: It runs synchronously in the mutation path; a filer.conf stored as chunks is fetched from volume servers inside the write that changed it.
Deleting filer.conf does not reset the rules: only events with a new entry trigger a reload, so the old rules stay until restart.
f.FilerConf is replaced without synchronization while writes read it.

weed/filer/meta_aggregator.go.character: MetaAggregator: following every peer filer's metadata log, merging it into one aggregated buffer and replicating peers' changes into this filer's store
weed/filer/meta_aggregator.go.what: OnPeerUpdate starts or stops a subscription loop per filer (itself included), reconnecting every 1.7 s after an error. doSubscribeToOneFiler reads the peer's store signature; a peer on a different store is replicated: its offset is read from KV (filer.meta.offset by signature) or, on first contact, the peer's whole tree is copied (traversePeerMetadata, excluding the system log) and the offset saved one minute before the copy began. It then calls SubscribeLocalMetadata (batching, idle heartbeats, log chunk refs read client-side), appends each event to MetaLogBuffer, replays it into the local store when the peer has a different store (replicateMetadataChange retries transient errors), runs onMetadataChangeEvent, and advances the peer's delivery and flush watermarks; the offset is persisted at most once a minute and on exit, clamped below the first event that failed to replay. Low watermarks across peers, change channels and RemotePeerArrivedChan let aggregated subscribers hold back until every peer has delivered or flushed a range.
weed/filer/meta_aggregator.go.why: Consequence: with several filers, each sees only its own mutations; subscribers and (for separate stores) the stores themselves need everyone's. Design: peers sharing one store only aggregate events, peers with their own stores also replay them; watermarks make the merged stream safe to resume.
weed/filer/meta_aggregator.go.when: Filers in a cluster with more than one filer (AggregateFromPeers at startup).
weed/filer/meta_aggregator.go.ux: A write through one filer is visible through all of them.
weed/filer/meta_aggregator.go.if_broken: Filers with separate stores diverge, or aggregated subscribers miss peer events.
gotchas: A replay that fails with a non-transient error is skipped for the rest of the session: only the persisted offset is held below it, so it is retried after a restart, not before.
Last-writer-wins between filers compares commit timestamps from different hosts' clocks, so clock skew decides conflicting writes.
Shutdown waits for every peer loop without a deadline, logging every 5 s.

weed/filer/meta_replay.go.character: Applying a peer filer's metadata event to the local store, newest commit wins
weed/filer/meta_replay.go.what: Replay locks the event's old and new paths exclusively and their ancestors shared, then: for an in-place update, skips it if the local commit is newer, else updates directories in place and replaces files; for a delete or rename source, skips if newer locally, else deletes (a directory's children are swept recursively, keeping any child committed locally after the event and any remote-only entry that took a path since the listing, deleting children's remote objects unless the delete was metadata-only or from another cluster, and their chunks in batches when the event deletes chunks); for a create or rename target, inserts unless the local commit is newer. Writes go straight to the store with the event's mutation timestamp as the commit stamp.
weed/filer/meta_replay.go.why: Consequence: two filers with separate stores receive each other's writes in an order that can differ from their own; applying blindly would let an older event overwrite a newer local write. Design: per-path commit timestamps decide, and a directory delete keeps the children that changed after it.
weed/filer/meta_replay.go.when: meta_aggregator.go for every event from a peer with a different store.
weed/filer/meta_replay.go.if_broken: Deleted files reappear on some filers, or newer writes are lost to older replicated ones.
gotchas: Replayed writes go to the store directly and publish no local event of their own; subscribers of the aggregated stream see the peer's event instead.
A child path held by a local mutation makes the sweep fail with ErrLockContended rather than wait.

weed/filer/meta_path_ts.go.character: Per-path commit timestamps for ordering replicated changes
weed/filer/meta_path_ts.go.what: CommitTsNs and EntryCommitTsNs return the entry's stored commit timestamp, or a fallback (the event time) for entries written before the field existed; localCommitTsNs uses the entry's mtime as that fallback and 0 for a missing entry.
weed/filer/meta_path_ts.go.why: Design: the commit timestamp is the version of a path; replay, bootstrap and the BFS traversal compare it to decide which side is newer.
weed/filer/meta_path_ts.go.if_broken: Replicated writes are applied out of order.
gotchas: For entries without a stored commit timestamp the comparison falls back to mtime in whole-second precision from the store.

weed/filer/metadata_event_context.go.character: Context flag that suppresses automatic metadata events
weed/filer/metadata_event_context.go.what: WithSuppressedMetadataEvents marks a context so NotifyUpdateEvent emits nothing for operations under it.
weed/filer/metadata_event_context.go.why: Design: a rename is implemented as creates and deletes; their individual events would look like a copy plus a delete to subscribers, so the rename publishes its own rename events after commit instead.
weed/filer/metadata_event_context.go.when: Rename's internal creates and deletes, rename target replacement.
weed/filer/metadata_event_context.go.ux: Mounts and replicas see a rename as a rename.
weed/filer/metadata_event_context.go.if_broken: Renames replicate as delete+create (losing hard-link and inode continuity), or produce duplicate events.

weed/filer/metadata_event_sink.go.character: Request-scoped capture of the metadata event a mutation produced
weed/filer/metadata_event_sink.go.what: WithMetadataEventSink attaches a sink to a context; NotifyUpdateEvent records each event into it, keeping the last; the RPC returns it in metadata_event.
weed/filer/metadata_event_sink.go.why: Consequence: a client that wrote an entry wants to update its own cache with the exact event (timestamp included) without waiting for the subscription to deliver it.
weed/filer/metadata_event_sink.go.when: CreateEntry, UpdateEntry, DeleteEntry and remote-cache RPCs.
weed/filer/metadata_event_sink.go.ux: Mounts see their own writes immediately.
weed/filer/metadata_event_sink.go.if_broken: Clients apply their own writes late or twice.
gotchas: Only the last event is kept; a recursive delete returns the directory's event, not its children's.

weed/filer/mount_peer_registry.go.character: In-memory registry of live weed mount peers for peer chunk sharing
weed/filer/mount_peer_registry.go.what: MountPeerRegistry maps a peer address to its data center, rack, last-seen and expiry. Register refreshes an entry (TTL defaults to 60 s, capped at one hour; new entries are refused beyond 10,000). List returns unexpired entries; Sweep deletes expired ones.
weed/filer/mount_peer_registry.go.why: Design: soft state rebuilt by heartbeats, bounded so a misbehaving client cannot grow it without limit.
weed/filer/mount_peer_registry.go.when: MountRegister / MountList RPCs and the filer's sweeper.
weed/filer/mount_peer_registry.go.if_broken: Mounts route chunk requests to dead peers or never find live ones.
gotchas: The registry is per filer and not replicated; mounts connected to different filers see different peer sets.

weed/filer/persisted_log_cache.go.character: LRU cache of decoded metadata-log chunks shared by all subscribers
weed/filer/persisted_log_cache.go.what: persistedLogCache keeps decoded LogEntry lists by chunk file id (256 MiB total, idle entries evicted after 5 minutes), loads each chunk once through singleflight under a 128 MiB load budget, and caches only chunks that decode completely (whole records, increasing timestamps); a partial chunk returns errLogChunkIncomplete so callers fall back to streaming.
weed/filer/persisted_log_cache.go.why: Consequence: many subscribers catching up over the same minutes refetched and re-decoded the same log chunks. Design: decode once, share; never cache a chunk that is still being appended to.
weed/filer/persisted_log_cache.go.when: LogFileIterator and LastShippedLogEntryTsNs during subscription catch-up.
weed/filer/persisted_log_cache.go.ux: Faster catch-up for many lagging subscribers.
weed/filer/persisted_log_cache.go.if_broken: Memory spikes during catch-up, or subscribers served a truncated chunk.
gotchas: Cached entry slices are shared between subscribers and must not be mutated.

weed/filer/topics.go.character: Paths of the topics tree and the system metadata log
weed/filer/topics.go.what: TopicsDir is /topics, SystemLogDir is /topics/.system/log (where every filer writes its per-minute metadata log), TopicConfFile is topic.conf.
weed/filer/topics.go.why: Design: the metadata log lives in the namespace itself, so it is stored and replicated like any file.
weed/filer/topics.go.when: Log flush and replay, event filtering (events under SystemLogDir are never published), traversals that exclude it.
weed/filer/topics.go.if_broken: Log files publish events about themselves (feedback loop) or are copied into backups.

weed/filer/remote_storage.go.character: Remote storage configuration and mount rules held by the filer
weed/filer/remote_storage.go.what: FilerRemoteStorage loads /etc/remote: each <name>.conf (a RemoteConf, optionally checked by a validator that rejects unsafe endpoints) and mount.mapping (local directory -> remote name, bucket, path), into a ptrie of mount directories; reloads are serialized and swapped in under a lock, and remote storage clients for removed confs are released. FindMountDirectory returns the deepest mount containing a path; FindRemoteStorageConf / GetRemoteStorageConf return its conf. ReadRemoteStorageConf, DetectMountInfo and UnmarshalRemoteStorageMappings serve shell commands.
weed/filer/remote_storage.go.why: Design: a remote mount makes a local directory a cache of a cloud bucket path; mounts and credentials are stored in the filer so every filer and tool sees the same set.
weed/filer/remote_storage.go.when: Startup and every /etc/remote change (filer_on_meta_event.go); every lookup under a mounted path.
weed/filer/remote_storage.go.if_broken: Mounted paths stop resolving to their remote, or a removed mount keeps being used.
gotchas: GetRemoteStorageClient / FindRemoteStorageClient build clients with remote_storage.GetRemoteStorage directly, bypassing the filer's guarded builder (BuildGuardedRemoteClient); nothing in this repository calls them, the filer paths use buildRemoteStorageClient.

weed/filer/remote_mapping.go.character: Read and edit the mount.mapping file
weed/filer/remote_mapping.go.what: FindMountedRemoteMapping picks the longest mapping containing a directory; ReadMountMappings reads the file; InsertMountMapping and DeleteMountMapping read it, add or remove one directory, and save it back.
weed/filer/remote_mapping.go.why: Design: one small protobuf file lists every remote mount.
weed/filer/remote_mapping.go.when: weed shell remote.mount / remote.unmount and related tools; the filer's remote-cache RPC.
gotchas: Insert and Delete are read-modify-write with the unconditional SaveInsideFiler; two concurrent mount edits can lose one.
addRemoteStorageMapping ignores an unmarshal error, so a corrupt mapping file is replaced by one holding only the new mapping.

weed/filer/read_remote.go.character: Remote-entry helpers: remote-only test, path mapping and the cache request
weed/filer/read_remote.go.what: IsInRemoteOnly is true for an entry with no chunks and a positive remote size. MergeRemoteContentEncoding copies the remote object's content encoding into the extended map (deleting it when the remote says none). MapFullPathToRemoteStorageLocation and MapRemoteStorageLocationPathToFullPath convert between a local path under a mount and the remote location. CacheRemoteObjectToLocalCluster asks a filer to cache an entry's bytes locally.
weed/filer/read_remote.go.why: Design: remote-only entries are metadata stubs whose bytes stay on the remote until cached.
weed/filer/read_remote.go.when: Lazy fetch and listing, deletes, renames, the S3 gateway and filer read paths deciding whether to cache first.
weed/filer/read_remote.go.if_broken: Remote objects resolve to the wrong remote key.
gotchas: MapFullPathToRemoteStorageLocation slices the path by the mount directory's length without checking it is under the mount.

weed/filer/filer_remote_evict.go.character: Finding locally cached remote objects that can be evicted
weed/filer/filer_remote_evict.go.what: IsEvictableRemoteEntry is true for a file with a remote copy, local chunks and a sync stamp no older than its mtime (no local change since it was synced). ListEvictableRemoteEntries walks every mount directory recursively through the store and returns such entries synced before a cutoff, oldest sync first. chunksEqual compares chunk lists by fid, size, offset and timestamp.
weed/filer/filer_remote_evict.go.why: Consequence: cached remote objects fill local volumes; only copies identical to the remote can be dropped safely. Design: the sync stamp proves the local chunks equal the remote object.
weed/filer/filer_remote_evict.go.when: The filer's remote-cache eviction when a cache write hits a capacity error (filer_grpc_server_remote.go reclaimRemoteCacheSpace).
weed/filer/filer_remote_evict.go.ux: Remote-mount caches shrink when volumes fill.
weed/filer/filer_remote_evict.go.if_broken: Local-only changes are evicted (data loss) or the cache never shrinks.
gotchas: The walk collects every candidate under every mount in memory before sorting.

weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote.go.character: On-demand materialization of remote-mount entries and remote deletes
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote.go.what: maybeLazyFetchFromRemote runs on a FindEntry miss under a remote mount: after the tombstone rebuild finishes and unless a delete is pending for the path, it stats the remote object (singleflight per path), creates any missing parent directories the same way, and persists a remote-only entry (mtime and size from the remote, content encoding merged), retracting it if a delete landed meanwhile. maybeDeleteFromRemote deletes a file's remote object or a directory's remote prefix; deleteSweptEntryRemote deletes only if the remote object is unchanged (conditional delete where supported, else stat-and-compare), releasing a pending rename source. RemoteSourcePath / RemoteReadPath follow ExtRemoteRenameSourceKey to where a renamed, not-yet-copied entry's bytes still live; CopyRemoteOnlyEntry and RemoteCopyLocations copy a remote-only object to a new key on the remote (refused out of the mount or for storage types without copy).
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote.go.why: Consequence: a remote mount can hold millions of objects; listing them all at mount time would be slow and stale. Design: entries appear when first looked up or listed, and a delete pending on the remote must not be resurrected by the next lookup.
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote.go.when: FindEntry misses and deletes under remote mounts; renames of remote-only entries.
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote.go.ux: S3 GET or mount access of an object that exists only in the mounted bucket works without a prior sync.
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote.go.if_broken: Remote objects invisible, deleted objects reappearing, or remote objects deleted while still referenced.
gotchas: A remote stat that fails for any reason is treated as 'not found', so a transient remote error makes the object look absent (404).
Misses are not cached: every lookup of a key absent locally under a mount calls the remote.

weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote_listing.go.character: Refreshing a remote-mount directory listing into the filer, with a per-directory TTL
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote_listing.go.what: maybeLazyListFromRemote, when the mount has a listing cache TTL and the directory's remote.listing.synced_at is older than it, lists the remote directory (singleflight per directory) and for each child creates a remote-only entry or directory, or refreshes an existing remote-backed entry's remote stamp, size, mtime and content encoding; entries without a remote stamp and paths with a pending delete are left alone. It then records the sync time on the directory.
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote_listing.go.why: Design: listing the remote on every directory read would be slow and costly; a TTL bounds staleness.
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote_listing.go.when: doListDirectoryEntries under remote mounts with ListingCacheTtlSeconds > 0.
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote_listing.go.ux: ls / S3 ListObjects on a remote mount shows remote objects added outside SeaweedFS within the TTL.
weed/filer/filer_lazy_remote_listing.go.if_broken: Remote additions never appear, or listings hammer the remote.
gotchas: Refreshed entries are written straight to the store with no metadata event, so subscribers (mount caches, peers) do not see listing-driven updates.
Store and remote errors are logged and swallowed; a failed listing looks like an unchanged directory.

weed/filer/filer_remote_tombstone.go.character: Tombstones that keep deleted remote-mount paths from being lazily resurrected until the remote delete is applied
weed/filer/filer_remote_tombstone.go.what: remoteDeletionTombstones records deleted files and directories (a directory covers its subtree) under remote mounts with the delete's commit stamp and, once its event lands, its stream position. isRemoteDeletionPending blocks lazy fetch and listing for a path until the write-back daemon's persisted sync offset for the mount passes that position, the path is written again, or 24 hours pass; a tombstone recorded before its event (pending) lifts only by its event or the TTL. When the table (65,536 paths) is full, all lazy fetches stay off until it drains. RebuildRemoteDeletionTombstones replays the persisted metadata log from the oldest sync offset at startup, gating lazy reads until done; onRemoteDeletionEvents maintains the table from the event stream.
weed/filer/filer_remote_tombstone.go.why: Consequence: deleting a file under a remote mount removes the local entry immediately, but filer.remote.sync deletes the remote object later; a lookup in between would recreate the entry from the remote. Design: track what is owed to the remote and lift it when the sync offset proves it was paid.
weed/filer/filer_remote_tombstone.go.when: Deletes under remote mounts, lazy fetch and listing, filer startup.
weed/filer/filer_remote_tombstone.go.ux: Deleted objects under a remote mount stay deleted.
weed/filer/filer_remote_tombstone.go.if_broken: Deleted remote-mount objects reappear, or lazy fetch stays disabled.
gotchas: Without a write-back daemon (no filer.remote.sync), every tombstone lasts the full 24 hours: an object recreated on the remote at a deleted path stays hidden that long.
Events still in the unflushed log tail at a crash are not replayed by the rebuild (author comment).

weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/cleanup_.character: Time-ordered, deduplicated queue of folders waiting to be checked for emptiness
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/cleanup_.what: CleanupQueue keeps one item per folder in a list ordered by event time, with a map for O(1) lookup. Add inserts or moves a folder to a newer time; Remove drops it (a create in the folder cancels its cleanup); PopOlderThan returns the oldest folder only once it has waited longer than the delay; ShouldProcess, Peek, Len, OldestAge and Contains support the processor and metrics.
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/cleanup_.why: Design: waiting a fixed delay after the last delete lets a burst of deletes and re-creates in one folder settle before anything checks it, and deduplication keeps one check per folder.
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/cleanup_.when: EmptyFolderCleaner.OnDeleteEvent / OnCreateEvent and its 30 s processor loop.
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/cleanup_.ux: Empty folders disappear about two minutes after their last object is deleted.
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/cleanup_.if_broken: Folders removed while still in use, or never removed.
gotchas: ShouldProcess's size trigger (1000 items) is not what the processor uses; it pops only items older than the delay.

weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/empty_fo.character: EmptyFolderCleaner: removing folders under buckets that become empty after deletes, with per-bucket opt-out and restore-on-race
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/empty_fo.what: Fed by delete, create and rename events (local and from peers), for folders at least one level below a bucket, outside .uploads, and owned by this filer on the DLM ring (one filer per folder). A delete that leaves the cached rough count at zero queues the folder; a create removes it. Every 30 s the processor takes folders queued longer than the delay (filer.options.s3.empty_folder_cleanup_delay in filer.toml, 2 minutes by default) and, if no create came after the last delete, loads the bucket's policy (cached 5 minutes, invalidated by bucket entry updates): the bucket attribute Seaweed-X-Amz-Allow-Empty-Folders=true opts out. It then counts entries (up to 1000), skips directories that are themselves objects (prefix objects, data) and S3 Tables catalog entries, remembers the folder's mode and owner, deletes it non-recursively, and recurses to the parent. A folder written to during or shortly after its delete (within a 2-minute observation window) is restored with its old attributes. Policy-load failures are retried up to 3 times.
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/empty_fo.why: Consequence: S3 has no real directories; after the last object under a/b/ is deleted, clients expect a/b/ to vanish from listings, but the filer keeps the directories it created implicitly. Design: event-driven and delayed, so busy folders are not churned; restore-on-race because a non-recursive delete can still interleave with a write into the folder from another filer.
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/empty_fo.when: Created by AggregateFromPeers on every filer; events arrive through onMetadataChangeEvent.
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/empty_fo.ux: Empty 'folders' disappear from S3 listings shortly after their contents are deleted; weed mount sets the opt-out on its buckets so mkdir'd empty directories survive.
weed/filer/empty_folder_cleanup/empty_fo.if_broken: Empty prefixes linger in listings (Spark and Hadoop clients see phantom directories), or folders are removed while objects are being written into them.
gotchas: Until the delay passes, the empty folder still exists and an S3 ListObjects with a delimiter returns it as a CommonPrefix (see the s3api_object_handlers_list.go flag).
State (rough counts, queue, deleted set) is in memory per filer; a restart forgets queued folders, which are then cleaned only by a later delete in them.
The folder delete is a filer delete like any other and publishes a metadata event; directories removed by the TTL expiry path in filer.go do not go through this cleaner.

weed/filer/filer_deletion.go.character: Asynchronous chunk deletion: the deletion queue, batch deletes on volume servers and the retry queue
weed/filer/filer_deletion.go.what: DeleteChunks queues a file's chunk ids (resolving manifest chunks to their data chunks first) unless the path's storage rule disables chunk deletion; DeleteChunksNotRecursive queues ids as given; deleteChunksIfNotNew queues what an update dropped. loopProcessingDeletion drains the queue every 1.1 s in batches of up to 100,000 unique ids, deletes them through the volume servers (locations from the master client's cache) and classifies each result: success and not-found leave the durable ledger; retryable errors (read-only volume, timeouts, lookup failures, rate limiting and similar text) go to DeletionRetryQueue with backoff from 5 minutes doubling to 6 hours; permanent errors are dropped. After 10 attempts an id is given up.
weed/filer/filer_deletion.go.why: Consequence: deleting needles synchronously in every write would tie metadata latency to volume servers. Design: metadata commits first, needles are deleted asynchronously and retried, and a durable ledger (filer_deletion_persist.go) makes the queue survive restarts.
weed/filer/filer_deletion.go.when: Every overwrite, delete and rename that frees chunks; the filer process background loop.
weed/filer/filer_deletion.go.ux: Space is reclaimed after deletes (after volume vacuum).
weed/filer/filer_deletion.go.if_broken: Disk space never reclaimed, or chunks still referenced deleted.
gotchas: Ids that exhaust their retries, or fail with a non-retryable error, are forgotten and stay on disk as orphans until volume.fsck.
If a manifest chunk cannot be resolved, the manifest itself is still deleted while its data chunks are not, leaking them.
Retryable versus permanent is decided by matching error text.

weed/filer/filer_deletion_persist.go.character: Durable ledger of chunk ids queued for deletion but not yet confirmed gone
weed/filer/filer_deletion_persist.go.what: Every queued id is recorded in an in-memory pending set with an epoch; terminal outcomes remove it (an expiry only removes a matching epoch, so a re-queued id survives). The set is snapshotted to the store's KV under filer.deleteQueue.ledger.v1 plus this filer's address when it changes, every 10 s and on shutdown, split into 64 KiB parts written per generation with the manifest published last; an index of ledger keys lets a filer restarted under a new address claim its old ledger. On startup the ledger is reloaded and its ids re-queued after a 30 s grace, so a peer still aggregating metadata can re-reference a chunk first. A failed startup read blocks snapshots until a read succeeds, so an unread ledger is never overwritten. Settings: filer.deleteQueue.persist, .persistInterval, .recoveryGrace.
weed/filer/filer_deletion_persist.go.why: Consequence: a crash between queuing a delete and the volume confirming it used to leak the chunk forever. Design: additive on enqueue, subtractive only on terminal outcomes, idempotent volume deletes absorb replays.
weed/filer/filer_deletion_persist.go.when: SetStore at startup, every queueDeletions, the snapshot timer and shutdown.
weed/filer/filer_deletion_persist.go.ux: Space from deletes is reclaimed even across filer restarts.
weed/filer/filer_deletion_persist.go.if_broken: Leaked chunks after crashes, or the ledger overwriting itself with a partial set.
gotchas: Re-queued ledger ids are deleted after the grace without re-checking that no entry references them; correctness relies on the ledger only ever holding chunks that metadata had already dropped.
